Input data: AMORIS (longitudinal) dvs results_dt från BA_rate_L.rmd

SENSITIVITY VERSION — reviewer comment 8 (secular assay drift 1985–1996).
Identical to Trajectories_binned__L.Rmd except that every model is additionally
adjusted for calendar year of measurement (derived from Provtagningsdatum), and
all output files get the suffix in `TAG` so the original run is not overwritten.

# 0.0 Calendar-year adjustment set-up (NEW)

## 0.1 Settings + deriving calendar year from Provtagningsdatum
```{r}
# Paths, output locations and analysis parameters come from config.R in the
# repository root. Nothing below hardcodes a location.
source(here::here("config.R"))

library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)

TAG     <- "_calyearadj"   # suffix on ALL output files -> original run stays intact
CAL_ADJ <- "linear"        # "linear" (default) | "factor" | "none"
                           #  linear = constant drift per calendar year
                           #  factor = year-specific step changes (reagent/instrument switches)
                           #  none   = reproduces the original model, for a sanity check

# --- Calendar year of measurement (decimal, so within-year timing is kept) ---
prov_date <- as.Date(results_dt$Provtagningsdatum)

results_dt$cal_year <- as.numeric(format(prov_date, "%Y")) +
  (as.numeric(format(prov_date, "%j")) - 1) / 365.25

# Centred: the intercept then means "fitted value at the AVERAGE calendar year",
# i.e. it keeps the same interpretation/scale as in the original model, so ALL
# downstream plotting code (which uses coef(fit)["(Intercept)"]) works unchanged.
results_dt$cal_year_c <- results_dt$cal_year - mean(results_dt$cal_year, na.rm = TRUE)

# Factor version with sum-to-zero contrasts -> intercept = average across years,
# again so the plotting code does not have to change.
results_dt$cal_year_f <- factor(floor(results_dt$cal_year))
contrasts(results_dt$cal_year_f) <- contr.sum(nlevels(results_dt$cal_year_f))

# --- The single term that gets pasted into every model formula below ---
cal_term <- switch(CAL_ADJ,
                   none   = "",
                   linear = " + cal_year_c",
                   factor = " + cal_year_f")

# --- Sanity checks ---
cat("Calendar year range:", range(floor(results_dt$cal_year), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Rows with missing Provtagningsdatum:",
    sum(is.na(results_dt$cal_year)), "of", nrow(results_dt), "\n")
cat("Correlation age vs calendar year:",
    round(cor(results_dt$age, results_dt$cal_year, use = "complete.obs"), 3), "\n\n")
print(table(floor(results_dt$cal_year), useNA = "ifany"))

# NOTE: rows with a missing date are dropped by lm(), which would make this run
# use slightly fewer observations than the original. If the count above is > 0,
# uncomment the next line so both runs use exactly the same rows:
# results_dt <- results_dt[!is.na(results_dt$cal_year), ]
```

## 0.2 Helper: pull the drift estimate out of any fitted model
```{r}
#Returns the calendar-year coefficient(s) with cluster-robust SEs.
#This IS the number to quote to the reviewer: estimated assay/secular drift
#in biological-age units per calendar year.
cal_drift <- function(fit, cluster, label) {
  co  <- coef(fit)
  idx <- grep("^cal_year", names(co))
  if (!length(idx)) return(NULL)
  vc  <- sandwich::vcovCL(fit, cluster = cluster)
  est <- co[idx]
  se  <- sqrt(diag(vc)[idx])
  data.frame(
    model     = label,
    term      = names(est),
    estimate  = round(est, 4),
    se        = round(se, 4),
    lower_CI  = round(est - 1.96 * se, 4),
    upper_CI  = round(est + 1.96 * se, 4),
    p_value   = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)), 3),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

drift_list <- list()   # filled in by the model chunks below
lbl <- function(outcome, d) {
  g  <- unique(as.character(d$gender))
  sx <- if (length(g) > 1) "both sexes"
        else if (g %in% c("2", "Women")) "women"
        else if (g %in% c("1", "Men")) "men" else g
  sprintf("%s (%s; n_obs=%d, n_id=%d)", outcome, sx, nrow(d), dplyr::n_distinct(d$sampleID))
}
```

# 2.0 Calculating trajectories binned by 5 years

## 2.1 Phenoage
```{r}
# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# --- Step 1: Prepare the data ---
to1po2_clean <- to1po2_men %>% #results_dt for all or to1po2_FH for only those with health checkups
  filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(phenoage)) %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    age_bin = cut(
      age,
      #breaks = seq(floor(min(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
      #             ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
      #             by = 5),
      breaks = seq(17, ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)), by = 5),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

# --- Step 2: Fit the model with interaction terms ---
fit <- lm(as.formula(paste0("phenoage ~ age + age:age_bin", cal_term)),   # CHANGED: + calendar year
          data = to1po2_clean)
coefs <- coef(fit)
vcov_clustered <- vcovCL(fit, cluster = to1po2_clean$sampleID)
drift_list[["phe_main"]] <- cal_drift(fit, to1po2_clean$sampleID, lbl("PhenoAge", to1po2_clean))

# --- Step 3: Global Wald test ---
interaction_terms <- grep("age:age_bin", names(coefs))
estimates <- coefs[interaction_terms]
V <- vcov_clustered[interaction_terms, interaction_terms]

wald_stat <- t(estimates) %*% solve(V) %*% estimates
df <- length(estimates)
p_value <- 1 - pchisq(wald_stat, df)

# --- Step 4: Compute slope estimates and confidence intervals ---
z <- 1.96
slope_table <- data.frame(
  age_bin = levels(to1po2_clean$age_bin),
  slope = NA,
  se = NA,
  lower_CI = NA,
  upper_CI = NA
)
library(stringr)

# Extract start and stop values from age_bin labels
bounds <- str_extract_all(slope_table$age_bin, "[0-9.]+")
slope_table$start <- as.numeric(sapply(bounds, `[`, 1))
slope_table$stop <- as.numeric(sapply(bounds, `[`, 2))

# Reference bin (first bin)
base_slope <- coefs["age"]
base_se <- sqrt(vcov_clustered["age", "age"])

slope_table[1, "slope"] <- base_slope
slope_table[1, "se"] <- base_se
slope_table[1, "lower_CI"] <- base_slope - z * base_se
slope_table[1, "upper_CI"] <- base_slope + z * base_se

# All other bins
for (i in 2:nrow(slope_table)) {
  bin <- slope_table$age_bin[i]
  term <- paste0("age:age_bin", bin)

  est <- base_slope + coefs[term]

  var_base <- vcov_clustered["age", "age"]
  var_int  <- vcov_clustered[term, term]
  covar    <- 2 * vcov_clustered["age", term]
  se <- sqrt(var_base + var_int + covar)

  slope_table[i, "slope"] <- est
  slope_table[i, "se"] <- se
  slope_table[i, "lower_CI"] <- est - z * se
  slope_table[i, "upper_CI"] <- est + z * se
}

# --- Output ---
cat("===== GLOBAL TEST (Wald) =====\n")
cat("Wald statistic:", round(wald_stat, 3), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", df, "\n")
cat("P-value:", paste0("< ", .Machine$double.eps), "\n\n")

cat("===== SLOPE ESTIMATES BY AGE BIN =====\n")
print(slope_table)

slope_table_all_phe <- slope_table
```

```{r}
write.table(as.data.frame(slope_table),
            file = out_path(paste0("trajectory_table_phe_men_calyear", TAG, ".csv")),
            sep = ";",
            dec = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE,
            fileEncoding = "Latin1") 
```

```{r}
# Create a one-row summary table with global Wald test output
wald_summary <- data.frame(
  wald_statistic = as.numeric(wald_stat),
  degrees_of_freedom = df,
  p_value = as.numeric(p_value)
)

print(wald_summary)
```

```{r}
            file = out_path(paste0("trajectory_table_wald_phe_men_calyear", TAG, ".csv")),
            sep = ";",

            quote = FALSE,
            fileEncoding = "Latin1") 
```

## 2.2 Creating figure (PhenoAge, density)
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(MASS)
library(fields)

# Assume slope_table, to1po2_clean, and fit already exist

# Extract global intercept from model
intercept <- coef(fit)["(Intercept)"]

# Construct CI-based rotated rectangles
plot_data <- slope_table %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    x0 = start,
    x1 = stop,
    y0 = intercept + slope * x0,
    y1 = intercept + slope * x1,

    dx = x1 - x0,
    dy = y1 - y0,
    L = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2),

    nx = -dy / L,
    ny = dx / L,

    slope_ci = (upper_CI - lower_CI) / 2,
    w = slope_ci * dx / sqrt(1 + slope^2),

    xA = x0 + w * nx,
    yA = y0 + w * ny,
    xB = x1 + w * nx,
    yB = y1 + w * ny,
    xC = x1 - w * nx,
    yC = y1 - w * ny,
    xD = x0 - w * nx,
    yD = y0 - w * ny,

    label_x = (x0 + x1) / 2,
    label_y = (y0 + y1) / 2,
    label = sprintf("%.2f", slope),
    group = paste0("bin_", start)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_data <- plot_data %>%
  filter(stop <= 82)

# Long-format polygon
polygon_df <- plot_data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do(data.frame(
    group = .$group,
    x = c(.$xA, .$xB, .$xC, .$xD),
    y = c(.$yA, .$yB, .$yC, .$yD)
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

# Optional spaghetti overlay toggle
show_spaghetti <- TRUE

# Start ggplot
phenoage_plot <- ggplot()

# Add spaghetti first (behind everything)
if (show_spaghetti) {
  set.seed(42)
  subset_ids <- sample(
    unique(to1po2_clean$sampleID),
    floor(0.01 * length(unique(to1po2_clean$sampleID)))
  )

  spaghetti_df <- to1po2_clean %>%
    filter(sampleID %in% subset_ids)

  # Same density approach as your previous KDM plot, adapted to phenoage
  add_kde_density <- function(df, x = "age", y = "phenoage", n = 250) {
    xx <- df[[x]]
    yy <- df[[y]]

    ok <- is.finite(xx) & is.finite(yy)

    out <- df
    out$dens <- NA_real_

    if (sum(ok) < 2 || length(unique(xx[ok])) < 2 || length(unique(yy[ok])) < 2) {
      return(out)
    }

    kde <- MASS::kde2d(xx[ok], yy[ok], n = n)
    surf <- list(x = kde$x, y = kde$y, z = kde$z)

    out$dens[ok] <- fields::interp.surface(surf, cbind(xx[ok], yy[ok]))
    out
  }

  spag_d <- spaghetti_df %>%
    add_kde_density(x = "age", y = "phenoage", n = 250) %>%
    group_by(sampleID) %>%
    arrange(age, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      xend = lead(age),
      yend = lead(phenoage),
      dens_seg = (dens + lead(dens)) / 2
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(xend), !is.na(yend), !is.na(dens_seg))

  phenoage_plot <- phenoage_plot +
    # tiny observation dots first
    geom_point(
      data = spaghetti_df,
      aes(x = age, y = phenoage),
      alpha = 0.50,
      size = 0.10,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # density-colored spaghetti segments
    geom_segment(
      data = spag_d,
      aes(x = age, y = phenoage, xend = xend, yend = yend, color = dens_seg),
      linewidth = 0.3,
      alpha = 0.30,
      lineend = "round",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    guides(color = "none")
}

# Add rotated CI rectangles, lines, and slope labels
phenoage_plot <- phenoage_plot +
  geom_polygon(
    data = polygon_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, group = group),
    fill = "darkred", alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = plot_data,
    aes(x = x0, xend = x1, y = y0, yend = y1),
    color = "darkred", size = 1
  ) +
  ggtext::geom_richtext(
    data = plot_data,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label),
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black",
    fill = alpha("white", 0.4),
    label.color = NA,
    vjust = -2,
    hjust = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(15, 85), ylim = c(15, 100)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 85, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 100, by = 10)) +
  labs(x = "Chronological Age", y = "PhenoAge") +
  theme_minimal()

print(phenoage_plot)
```
```{r}
pdf(fig_path("trajectory_men_phe_calyear.pdf"), 
    width = 6, height = 6)
print(phenoage_plot)  # Send plot to file
dev.off()  # Close device
```

## 2.3 KDM
```{r}
# Load required packages
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# --- Step 1: Prepare the data ---
to1po2_clean <- to1po2_men %>% #results_dt for all or to1po2_FH for those with health checkups, MAIN results_dt
  filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(kdm)) %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    age_bin = cut(
      age,
      #breaks = seq(floor(min(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
      #             ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
      #             by = 5),
      breaks = seq(17, ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)), by = 5),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

# --- Step 2: Fit the model with interaction terms ---
fit <- lm(as.formula(paste0("kdm ~ age + age:age_bin", cal_term)),        # CHANGED: + calendar year
          data = to1po2_clean)
coefs <- coef(fit)
vcov_clustered <- vcovCL(fit, cluster = to1po2_clean$sampleID)
drift_list[["phe_main"]] <- cal_drift(fit, to1po2_clean$sampleID, lbl("PhenoAge", to1po2_clean))  # NEW

# --- Step 3: Global Wald test ---
interaction_terms <- grep("age:age_bin", names(coefs))
estimates <- coefs[interaction_terms]
V <- vcov_clustered[interaction_terms, interaction_terms]

wald_stat <- t(estimates) %*% solve(V) %*% estimates
df <- length(estimates)
p_value <- 1 - pchisq(wald_stat, df)

# --- Step 4: Compute slope estimates and confidence intervals ---
z <- 1.96
slope_table <- data.frame(
  age_bin = levels(to1po2_clean$age_bin),
  slope = NA,
  se = NA,
  lower_CI = NA,
  upper_CI = NA
)

library(stringr)

# Extract start and stop values from age_bin labels
bounds <- str_extract_all(slope_table$age_bin, "[0-9.]+")
slope_table$start <- as.numeric(sapply(bounds, `[`, 1))
slope_table$stop <- as.numeric(sapply(bounds, `[`, 2))

# Reference bin (first bin)
base_slope <- coefs["age"]
base_se <- sqrt(vcov_clustered["age", "age"])

slope_table[1, "slope"] <- base_slope
slope_table[1, "se"] <- base_se
slope_table[1, "lower_CI"] <- base_slope - z * base_se
slope_table[1, "upper_CI"] <- base_slope + z * base_se

# All other bins
for (i in 2:nrow(slope_table)) {
  bin <- slope_table$age_bin[i]
  term <- paste0("age:age_bin", bin)
  
  est <- base_slope + coefs[term]
  
  var_base <- vcov_clustered["age", "age"]
  var_int  <- vcov_clustered[term, term]
  covar    <- 2 * vcov_clustered["age", term]
  se <- sqrt(var_base + var_int + covar)
  
  slope_table[i, "slope"] <- est
  slope_table[i, "se"] <- se
  slope_table[i, "lower_CI"] <- est - z * se
  slope_table[i, "upper_CI"] <- est + z * se
}

# --- Step 5: Ensure numeric and round all numeric columns ---
slope_table <- slope_table %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

# --- Output ---
cat("===== GLOBAL TEST (Wald) =====\n")
cat("Wald statistic:", round(wald_stat, 3), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", df, "\n")
cat("P-value:", paste0("< ", .Machine$double.eps), "\n\n")

cat("===== SLOPE ESTIMATES BY AGE BIN =====\n")
```

# 3.0 Statistical sex differences in trajectories

## 3.1 PhenoAge
```{r}
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)
library(stringr)

# -----------------------------
# 1. Prepare data
# -----------------------------
to1po2_clean <- results_dt %>%
  filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(phenoage), !is.na(gender)) %>%
  group_by(sampleID) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    age_bin = cut(
      age,
      breaks = seq(17, ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)), by = 5),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      right = FALSE
    ),
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Men", "Women"))
  )

# -----------------------------
# 2. Fit joint model
# -----------------------------
fit <- lm(as.formula(paste0("phenoage ~ age * age_bin * gender", cal_term)),  # CHANGED: + calendar year
          data = to1po2_clean)

# Cluster-robust covariance matrix
vc <- vcovCL(fit, cluster = to1po2_clean$sampleID)
drift_list[["PhenoAge (sex model)"]] <- drift_list[["phe_main"]] <- cal_drift(fit, to1po2_clean$sampleID, lbl("PhenoAge", to1po2_clean))  # NEW

# Coefficients
coefs <- coef(fit)

# Optional: inspect coefficient names if debugging
# print(names(coefs))

# -----------------------------
# 3. Compute slopes and sex differences by age bin
# -----------------------------
z <- 1.96
bins <- levels(to1po2_clean$age_bin)

out <- data.frame(
  age_bin = bins,
  slope_men = NA_real_,
  slope_women = NA_real_,
  diff_women_minus_men = NA_real_,
  lower_CI = NA_real_,
  upper_CI = NA_real_,
  p_value = NA_real_
)

for (i in seq_along(bins)) {
  
  bin <- bins[i]
  
  # Term names
  term_age_bin <- paste0("age:age_bin", bin)
  term_gender  <- "age:genderWomen"
  term_three   <- paste0("age:age_bin", bin, ":genderWomen")
  
  # Base age slope
  beta_age <- coefs["age"]
  
  # Age-bin slope deviation (0 for reference bin)
  beta_bin <- if (term_age_bin %in% names(coefs)) coefs[term_age_bin] else 0
  
  # Women vs men slope difference in reference bin
  beta_gender <- if (term_gender %in% names(coefs)) coefs[term_gender] else 0
  
  # Additional women vs men slope difference in this bin
  beta_three <- if (term_three %in% names(coefs)) coefs[term_three] else 0
  
  # Slopes
  slope_men <- beta_age + beta_bin
  slope_women <- beta_age + beta_bin + beta_gender + beta_three
  
  # Difference: women - men
  diff <- beta_gender + beta_three
  
  # Variance of difference
  if (term_three %in% rownames(vc)) {
    var_diff <- vc[term_gender, term_gender] +
      vc[term_three, term_three] +
      2 * vc[term_gender, term_three]
  } else {
    var_diff <- vc[term_gender, term_gender]
  }
  
  se_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)
  lower <- diff - z * se_diff
  upper <- diff + z * se_diff
  p <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(diff / se_diff))
  
  out[i, ] <- list(
    bin,
    slope_men,
    slope_women,
    diff,
    lower,
    upper,
    p
  )
}

# -----------------------------
# 4. Clean supplement table
# -----------------------------
supp_table <- out %>%
  mutate(
    age_bin = gsub("\\[|\\)", "", age_bin),
    age_bin = gsub(",", "-", age_bin),
    slope_men = round(slope_men, 4),
    slope_women = round(slope_women, 4),
    diff_women_minus_men = round(diff_women_minus_men, 4),
    lower_CI = round(lower_CI, 4),
    upper_CI = round(upper_CI, 4),
    p_value = ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p_value))
  )

sex_difference_trajectories_phe <- supp_table %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `Age interval` = age_bin,
    `Slope men` = slope_men,
    `Slope women` = slope_women,
    `Difference (women - men)` = diff_women_minus_men,
    `Lower CI` = lower_CI,
    `Upper CI` = upper_CI,
    `P-value` = p_value
  )

print(sex_difference_trajectories_phe)
```
```{r}
write.table(as.data.frame(sex_difference_trajectories_phe),
            file = out_path(paste0("sex_difference_trajectories_phe_calyear", TAG, ".csv")),
            sep = ";",
            dec = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE,
            fileEncoding = "Latin1") 
```

## 4.2 Drift in the raw biomarkers themselves
```{r}
# The most direct evidence on assay drift: does the raw analyte level shift
# across 1985-1996 once age and sex are held constant? Reuses the same
# `biomarkers` vector as Calculating_BA_L.rmd.
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)

biomarkers_chk <- intersect(
  c("S_Alb", "S_Krea", "TC", "TG", "S_K", "S_Urea",
    "S_LD", "S_Ca", "S_Urat", "S_FAMN", "S_Hapt", "fS_Gluk"),
  names(results_dt)
)
cat("Biomarkers found in results_dt:", paste(biomarkers_chk, collapse = ", "), "\n")

biomarker_drift <- lapply(biomarkers_chk, function(b) {
  d <- results_dt %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[b]]), !is.na(cal_year_c), !is.na(age), !is.na(gender))
  if (nrow(d) < 100) return(NULL)

  f  <- lm(as.formula(paste0("`", b, "` ~ age + factor(gender) + cal_year_c")), data = d)
  v  <- sandwich::vcovCL(f, cluster = d$sampleID)
  est <- coef(f)["cal_year_c"]
  se  <- sqrt(v["cal_year_c", "cal_year_c"])
  mu  <- mean(d[[b]], na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    biomarker            = b,
    n_obs                = nrow(d),
    mean_level           = round(mu, 3),
    drift_per_year       = round(est, 4),
    se                   = round(se, 4),
    lower_CI             = round(est - 1.96 * se, 4),
    upper_CI             = round(est + 1.96 * se, 4),
    pct_of_mean_per_year = round(100 * est / mu, 3),
    p_value              = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(est / se)), 3),
    row.names            = NULL
  )
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

print(biomarker_drift)

write.table(as.data.frame(biomarker_drift),
            file = out_path(paste0("calendar_year_drift_biomarkers", TAG, ".csv")),
            sep = ";",
            dec = ",",
            row.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE,
            fileEncoding = "Latin1")
```

## 4.3 Figure: age- and sex-standardised annual biomarker levels
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Age- and sex-adjusted annual means (residuals + intercept), scaled to the
# overall mean so all biomarkers can be shown on one panel grid.
annual_levels <- lapply(biomarkers_chk, function(b) {
  d <- results_dt %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[b]]), !is.na(cal_year), !is.na(age), !is.na(gender))
  if (nrow(d) < 100) return(NULL)

  f <- lm(as.formula(paste0("`", b, "` ~ age + factor(gender)")), data = d)
  d$adj <- resid(f) + mean(d[[b]], na.rm = TRUE)

  d %>%
    mutate(year = floor(cal_year)) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(
      biomarker = b,
      n         = dplyr::n(),
      mean_adj  = mean(adj, na.rm = TRUE),
      se        = sd(adj, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
      .groups   = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      rel      = 100 * mean_adj / mean(mean_adj),
      rel_low  = 100 * (mean_adj - 1.96 * se) / mean(mean_adj),
      rel_high = 100 * (mean_adj + 1.96 * se) / mean(mean_adj)
    )
}) %>% dplyr::bind_rows()

drift_plot <- ggplot(annual_levels, aes(x = year, y = rel)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = rel_low, ymax = rel_high), fill = "darkred", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(color = "darkred") +
  geom_point(color = "darkred", size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ biomarker, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Calendar year of measurement",
       y = "Age- and sex-adjusted level (% of biomarker mean)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(drift_plot)
```

```{r}
pdf(fig_path("trajectory_all_phe_driftplot.pdf"), 
    width = 6, height = 6)
print(drift_plot)  # Send plot to file
dev.off()  # Close device
```

# 5.0 Calendar-year check against the current trajectory model

Sections 2.1 and 2.3 above use the earlier shared-intercept specification
(`age + age:age_bin`). The trajectories reported in Supplementary Tables 4-5
use bin-specific intercepts (`age * age_bin`). This section refits that
current model with and without calendar year, on identical rows, and reports
the change in each slope for the 13 reported bins (17-82 years). This is the
comparison quoted in the response to Reviewer 3 (comment 8).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(sandwich)

bin_breaks <- seq(17, ceiling(max(results_dt$age, na.rm = TRUE)), by = 5)  # same bins as the main analysis

slopes_by_bin <- function(fit, vc) {
  co <- coef(fit); bins <- levels(model.frame(fit)$age_bin)
  out <- t(sapply(bins, function(b) {
    term <- paste0("age:age_bin", b)
    if (b == bins[1]) c(co["age"], sqrt(vc["age", "age"]))
    else c(co["age"] + co[term], sqrt(vc["age", "age"] + vc[term, term] + 2 * vc["age", term]))
  }))
  colnames(out) <- c("slope", "se"); out
}

compare_calyear <- function(data, ba, label) {
  d <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(age), !is.na(.data[[ba]]), !is.na(cal_year_c)) %>%
    group_by(sampleID) %>% filter(n() >= 3) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(age_bin = cut(age, breaks = bin_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE))
  f0 <- lm(as.formula(paste(ba, "~ age * age_bin")), data = d)               # as in Supp. Tables 4-5
  f1 <- lm(as.formula(paste(ba, "~ age * age_bin + cal_year_c")), data = d)  # + linear calendar year
  s0 <- slopes_by_bin(f0, vcovCL(f0, cluster = d$sampleID))
  s1 <- slopes_by_bin(f1, vcovCL(f1, cluster = d$sampleID))
  keep <- as.numeric(sub(".*,([0-9.]+)[])]$", "\\1", rownames(s0))) <= 82
  data.frame(model = label, age_bin = rownames(s0)[keep],
             slope = round(s0[keep, "slope"], 4), slope_calyear = round(s1[keep, "slope"], 4),
             change = round(s1[keep, "slope"] - s0[keep, "slope"], 4), row.names = NULL)
}

calyear_check <- bind_rows(
  compare_calyear(results_dt,                           "kdm",      "KDM, all"),
  compare_calyear(results_dt[results_dt$gender == 1, ], "kdm",      "KDM, men"),
  compare_calyear(results_dt[results_dt$gender == 2, ], "kdm",      "KDM, women"),
  compare_calyear(results_dt,                           "phenoage", "PhenoAge, all"),
  compare_calyear(results_dt[results_dt$gender == 1, ], "phenoage", "PhenoAge, men"),
  compare_calyear(results_dt[results_dt$gender == 2, ], "phenoage", "PhenoAge, women")
)

print(calyear_check %>% group_by(model) %>% summarise(max_abs_change = max(abs(change))))
cat("Largest change in any slope (17-82 years):", max(abs(calyear_check$change)), "\n")

write.table(calyear_check, out_path(paste0("calyear_check_current_model", TAG, ".csv")),
            sep = ";", dec = ",", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, fileEncoding = "Latin1")
```
